data.title: CD
data.tagline: CD keeps verified versions continuously releasable, or releases them to production automatically under defined rules.
data.learningOutcome: You can see which environment a version reaches and tell whether production is human-approved or automatically released.
data.description: Continuous delivery keeps a version through the pipeline and ready to release, with a possible human approval before production. Continuous deployment automatically releases to production after gates pass. Both are more than “tests run automatically”; the key difference is whether production keeps a human approval.

learning.assumes: You know CI can provide build and test results for a commit.
learning.outcome: You can see which environment a version reaches and tell whether production is human-approved or automatically released.

distinctions.label: CI
distinctions.explanation: CD concerns how versions continuously reach target environments. CI concerns how changes integrate frequently and receive automated build and test feedback.

explanation.title: Continuous delivery retains the release decision
explanation.text: Versions build, test, and become releasable automatically; the team can still review testing, timing, and risk before approving production. Human approval does not make earlier verification manual.

explanation.title: Continuous deployment releases passing gates automatically
explanation.text: When a team explicitly uses continuous deployment, a version reaches production automatically after predefined checks. It needs reliable testing, monitoring, and stopping mechanisms; the label CD alone never proves automatic release is safe.

data.boundary: CD has two meanings: Continuous Delivery or Continuous Deployment. Both follow CI, but differ on whether production requires human approval. Automatically testing with no releasable or release step is not CD.

lessonPractice.title: After CI passes, a pipeline automatically deploys testing; a product owner checks the page and data, then clicks “release production.” Which kind of CD is this?

options.label: Continuous delivery, because production still has an explicit human approval
options.feedback: Correct. The version stays continuously releasable, but a person still decides to release it to production.

options.label: Continuous deployment, because testing deployment is automatic
options.feedback: Automatic testing deployment does not decide the name; the key is whether production releases automatically after gates pass.

options.label: Only CI, because the pipeline ran tests
options.feedback: A passing version is being made releasable and released, which goes beyond CI.

data.agentPrompt: Automatically deploy CI-passing versions to the test environment. Keep production as continuous delivery: show an explicit human approval step only after the test URL and key checks are confirmed; do not default to automatic production release.
